title: My Joy Is Heavy by The Bengsons #myjoyisheavy #thebengsons #nytw #the...
transcript: This was pretty devastating for having “joy” in its title. In their newest offering which started previews last night at New York Theatre Workshop, married musical duo The Bengsons chronicle their experience of trying to have a baby during the height of the pandemic. It's something that entails, as they describe it, “infinite love, no control.” Compared to the last piece I saw by them, this one is definitely more narrative than thematic. They still maintain their signature sound, poetic writing, and effortlessly captivating presence. Abigail Bengson's voice is really beautiful — it has a folky, resonant, and almost guttural quality, paired with impressive range and agility. She just exudes so much emotion, melding sadness with joy in a way that feels genuine and really invites you in. Overall, this feels like a cross between a warm hug and a catharsis, with every emotional beat earned. The production feels a little big for the story it tells, with some of the live projections with the detailed house set being a bit distracting. But aside from these tiny quibbles, I thought it was great — it is indeed joyful and heavy. With that, another program for my collection.
